briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-003
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- water tower top: (112, 113), roof
- workshop: (41, -69), indoor
- water tank: (-127, 15), outdoor
- fuel depot: (46, -119), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 9 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3300 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1380 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 9 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2460 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera.
- T2: Photograph workshop for the condition report. Location: workshop. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T3: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Photograph workshop for the condition report. Location: workshop. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera.
- T5: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: water tower top (112, 113, a rooftop); workshop (41, -69, indoors); water tank (-127, 15, outside); fuel depot (46, -119, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 9 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 55 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 7 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 23 minutes including the flight home. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 9 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 41 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Do a visual check of water tower top - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.
(T2) We need pictures of workshop for the report - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Get eyes on water tower top and check the panels - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T4) We need pictures of workshop for the report - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T5) Do a visual check of water tower top - that takes 1 minute on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
